newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAGACH CAUGHT CHEATING WITH DRUGS FOR SECOND TIME.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAGACH CAUGHT CHEATING WITH DRUGS FOR SECOND TIME.

text.p: Ukraine's world shot put champion Aleksandr Bagach has been stripped of his gold medal after being caught cheating with banned drugs for the second time.

The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) said on Thursday that the Olympic bronze medallist had tested positive for the stimulant ephedrine and would lose his gold medal and the $60,000 winner's prize.

French 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan, neither of whom made the finals, have also tested positive for ephedrine, the IAAF said. Their results have been cancelled.

As the IAAF softened their doping rules just before the championships, all three will receive a public warning but will be free to continue competing in lucrative grand prix meetings after the championships. They are the first drugs cases of the sixth world championships.

"Following the recent decision by the IAAF congress, these athletes will be issued a public warning and disqualified from the competition," the IAAF said in a statement. "The results they achieved at these world championships have been cancelled."

American John Godina, who received a wild card entry as defending champion, will now take the shot gold medal, German Oliver-Sven Buder the silver and another American, C.J. Hunter, fiancee of new world 100 metres champion Marion Jones, has been awarded the bronze.
Bagach was banned for two years in 1989 after he was found to have excessive levels of the male hormone testosterone in his body when he was competing for the former Soviet Union.
The 30-year-old athlete would have been banned for life if he had tested positive for a serious drug such as steroids.
Under the old rules, the shot putter would have been suspended for three months and missed the big-money European meetings in Zurich, Monaco, Brussels and Berlin in the next month.

But the IAAF's congress voted before the championships to change its rules on stimulants. It also cut its penalties for serious drugs such as steroids from four to two years because of legal problems.
Bagach equalled his personal best by recording 21.47 metres at his third attempt to win the competition in Athens on Saturday. He said afterwards that he could not believe his performance.

The Ukrainian struggled to make his way back to the top after being banned for two years for testosterone following third place in the 1989 European Cup in Gateshead, England. As a result, the Soviet team lost their place in the World Cup.

After his victory on Saturday, Ukraine's team leader Aleksandr Kolenko said: "Those were different times. Since, he has totally changed his approach to competition, trying to find a right balance between power and technique."
It is clear, however, that Bagach could not resist the temptation to cheat his way to glory again.
French officials said Maran had already left Athens and but could still face a tougher penalty from his national authority.
"The French federation has not changed its rules," French team doctor Herve de Labareyre said. "(But) He will probably face a suspended sentence from the French federation."
